items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Lucy는 무엇을 팔지 생각해 보겠다고 했다.
Minjun은 책을 판 돈으로 새 책을 살 것이다.
플리마켓은 이번 주 일요일 오전에 시작한다.
Lucy는 Minjun에게 책을 들어 달라고 부탁했다.
items.exp: 마지막에 Lucy가 I'll think about what to sell.이라고 했어요. Minjun은 책을 팔아서 번 돈을 기부할 예정이고(donate), 행사는 토요일 오후에 시작해요.
items.passage:
G: Hey, Minjun, those books look so heavy. Can I give you a hand?
B: Thank you, Lucy. You're so kind!
G: No problem. Why are you carrying so many books?
B: I'm going to sell them in a flea market and donate the money.
G: Wow, I want to join you.
B: Great. It starts this Saturday afternoon.
G: Okay, I'll think about what to sell.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: 한 할머니는 학생들이 떠난 뒤에 감사 인사를 했다.
학생들은 어르신들이 점심 식사하는 것을 도왔다.
학생들은 양로원 방을 청소해 달라는 부탁을 받았다.
items.exp: we helped the elderly people when they were having lunch라고 했어요. 할머니의 말은 Before we left, 즉 떠나기 전이었어요.
items.passage: G: Last Wednesday, our class did volunteer work. We visited a nursing home, and we cleaned the rooms. Also, we helped the elderly people when they were having lunch. Before we left, an elderly woman told me, "Thanks to you, I had a wonderful day. I really appreciate your help." It was a meaningful experience.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [having]의 have와 같은 의미로 쓰인 문장은?
items.exp: having lunch의 have는 '먹다'예요. has breakfast가 같아요. 나머지는 가지다, (병에) 걸려 있다, 있다예요.
items.passage: G: Last Wednesday, our class did volunteer work. We visited a nursing home, and we cleaned the rooms. Also, we helped the elderly people when they were [having] lunch. Before we left, an elderly woman told me, "Thanks to you, I had a wonderful day. I really appreciate your help." It was a meaningful experience.

items.q:
글의 흐름상 다음 문장이 들어갈 위치로 가장 알맞은 곳은?
Also, we helped the elderly people when they were having lunch.
items.exp: Also는 앞의 활동(방 청소)에 이어 다른 활동을 덧붙일 때 쓰고, 떠나기 전에 있던 일인 할머니의 말 앞에 와야 해요.
items.passage: G: ① Last Wednesday, our class did volunteer work. ② We visited a nursing home, and we cleaned the rooms. ③ Before we left, an elderly woman told me, "Thanks to you, I had a wonderful day." ④ It was a meaningful experience. ⑤

items.q: 밑줄 친 [when they were having lunch]의 when과 쓰임이 같은 when이 쓰인 문장은?
choices: I was cooking [when] my father came home.
I don't know [when] the bus comes.
The question is [when] we will start.
items.exp: 대화의 when은 '~할 때'라는 시간 접속사예요. 나머지 보기의 when은 '언제'를 뜻하는 의문사예요.
items.passage: G: Last Wednesday, our class did volunteer work. We visited a nursing home, and we cleaned the rooms. Also, we helped the elderly people [when] they were having lunch. Before we left, an elderly woman told me, "Thanks to you, I had a wonderful day. I really appreciate your help." It was a meaningful experience.

items.q: 글쓴이가 이 활동을 되돌아보는 느낌으로 가장 알맞은 것은?
items.exp: 마지막 문장 It was a meaningful experience.와 할머니의 감사 인사로 보아 보람을 느끼고 있어요.
items.passage: G: Last Wednesday, our class did volunteer work. We visited a nursing home, and we cleaned the rooms. Also, we helped the elderly people when they were having lunch. Before we left, an elderly woman told me, "Thanks to you, I had a wonderful day. I really appreciate your help." It was a meaningful experience.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: A, B, C는 D에게 자전거를 빌려주려 한다.
D는 비 때문에 자전거를 못 탄다.
B가 날씨를 바꿀 수 있다고 했다.
D는 눈이 와서 자전거를 탈 수 없다.
items.exp: D가 I want to ride my bike, but it's snowing.이라고 했고, 날씨를 바꿀 수 있다고 한 사람은 A예요.
items.passage:
A, B, C: What's the matter?
D: I want to ride my bike, but it's snowing.
A: Can I give you a hand? I can change the weather.
D: I really appreciate your help.

items.q: 밑줄 친 [it's snowing]의 it과 쓰임이 같은 it이 쓰인 문장은?
choices: I bought a new phone. [It] is red.
I love this song. I listen to [it] every day.
He found [it] hard to open the door.
items.exp: it's snowing의 it은 날씨를 나타내는 비인칭 주어이고, 어두워지는 것도 같은 비인칭 주어예요. 나머지는 대명사, 가주어, 목적어, 가목적어예요.
items.passage:
A, B, C: What's the matter?
D: I want to ride my bike, but [it's] snowing.
A: Can I give you a hand? I can change the weather.
D: I really appreciate your help.

items.q: 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: When did you learn to ride?
items.exp: 뒤에서 D가 문제 상황(눈 때문에 자전거를 못 탐)을 말하므로 무슨 일이냐고 묻는 말이 알맞아요.

items.exp: I can change the weather.의 can은 '~할 수 있다'는 능력이에요. 나머지는 허락, 요청, 가능성이에요.

items.exp: Can I give you a hand?는 '도와줄까?'라는 도움 제안 표현이에요. hand는 '손'이 아니라 '도움'을 뜻해요.

items.q: 윗글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
